page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server delivers 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 80 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and features a cache hierarchy including 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is configured with 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This resource density represents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute capacity over large memory footprints. Additionally, the server does not include local storage, relying instead on external Premium Storage options, and features no integrated GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the D160als_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench and PassMark CPU suites. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 14528.43 GB/sec and uncached large-block write bandwidth of 210.18 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, it processes Redis SET operations at 202.7 million operations per second and handles LLM inference for medium 7B models at 74.26 tokens per second in text generation. This high compute density offers qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory allocations or local NVMe drives.

Given its high core count and compute-centric design, the D160als_v7 is optimized for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for batch processing and large-scale parallel computing tasks where memory requirements remain within the 2.0 GB per core boundary.
